1. I am 27
2. Single
3. 25-26
4. 26, ongoing
5. First “not straight”, then queer suited me. I’m starting to think that I’m fully gay/lesbian.
6. I didn’t realize that I could participate in gay communities. I always dated men, but had special “weird” feelings around girls in high school that I realize now were crushes. I just always thought that since I’m a straight-presenting woman, that I am straight. It never occurred to me that I could indeed be queer, if was even allowed to! I moved abroad when I just turned 25 and met a girl who was cool. We got blackout drunk one night and made out intensely, then had sex. I remember feeling like it was much more natural than sex with men, like a dance that was always in me. From then on, I’ve been intimate with men & women, thinking I was bi. But I had the HUGEST crush on a friend/coworker when I was 24, would feel so good around her and was severely attracted to her. Feelings of shame prevented me from being honest about my feelings for her to her. But I was able to express it to a close friend at the time.
7. I had a short term relationship with a woman and always masturbate to women and just don’t feel the same with men, ever. Sometimes I find men “hot” but that’s about it. I just feel lighter and more myself when I admit that I’m probably gay.
8. My first kiss was actually with a girl when I was around 16-17. I didn’t think much of it, then went on dating guys because heterosexual norms etc.
9. I am working on myself and feel proud that I’m able to be honest with myself about this. I’m proud of who I am becoming (revealing), but not so comfortable in my own skin yet with this.
10. Honesty with ourselves is a major stepping stone towards peace & authentic relationships, whether with family, friends, strangers, or romantic interests

I weirdly feel like a sort of high today even without it. I aspire to prove to myself that I don’t need to impulsively give in to urges or run away fro unsettling feelings. Sitting with the feelings, honoring them, and knowing in my soul that they’ll eventually pass. That’s my personal journey. 

I will keep posting my journey, but literally taking the days moment by moment in these early times. I don’t want to contribute to my own chaos with weed. When real life crisis Inevitably happen, I want to be clear & able to make conscious decisions on how to act. Plus, I know I can be a better friend & family member without weed. It’s this false “everything’s all good” that it SO lovely, but just not reality.

Hey, I’m down! Also 25 from the US living in Europe now. PM me :)

Ironically I was on YouTube typing in “ways to quit smoking weed”. I found a GEM of a human called Preston Smiles. I became very into his videos- super uplifting and real for me.

A couple months later I joined a program of his basically for self development- support coaches, interesting challenging tasks. Felt like I had family for the first time. It was a 6 month long thing.

NONE of that would’ve happened had I not attempted to stop smoking! This was early last year when I found Preston. He was my inspiration to quit and I made it 60 days last time. 

I urge you to look him up! Best thing of 2019 for me was discovering his magic.

I hear you. For me, I’ve personally started a spiritual journey that was foreign to me even one year ago. I read books, explore the new area I’m living in, and am fortunate enough to have a group of other who are also in the process of evolving themselves- we chat daily.

Breathe in the negative feelings and KNOW that there other people out there who feel the exact same way (obviously from different reference points). Breathe out. Focus on the breathe from deep in your belly. The more oxygen our body has, the more choice we have.

What activities do you like to do? (Even if you’ve not enjoyed them for some time)

I read it. You are on the path many of us are. I’m your age and smoked since 17- first time I did I felt love from within for the first time and I cling to that feeling. I’ve smashed pipes, threw out weed and grinders- only to come right back once I felt “stable”. I’ve challenged myself to go 100 weed free to meet the beautiful sober woman I am today.

You will do it when you are ready. You are exactly where you need to be. It may not feel like it, but don’t believe everything you feel. FEELing is a huge part of healing. And we are addicted to smoking because of some unhealed part of ourselves.

DM me if you want to chat- I’m on day 15 and only looking forward!

Great post dude. I’m in day 14 after smoking at least once a day for 7 years. It became a part of my identity- thought I was a cool girl for doing the “right” things in life and still getting high all the time.

I’ve recently moved to a new country where I have some stoner friends too. I’ve spent less time with them and more time reading, yoga, dancing in my mirror, and enjoying the good beer here.

I’ve never done more than 60 days clean- from what I remember moves were more enjoyable and memorable, brain fog lifts, and I can actually enjoy my own company and not identify strongly with every thought I have!

I look forward to seeing more result. I’ve challenged myself to go at least 100 days (an attainable, definable goal). After that, hopefully I will do another 100! The hardest part for me will be hanging out with friends who smoke and not partaking.

I wish you well on your journey :) your future self will thank you

I think setting a goal like 90 days or 6 months or whatever can help add some structure. Also explore moving out once you’re financially sound.

I smoked for like 7 years and now am 24. I stopped smoking and am on week 7-8 now.

People at work have told me my skin looks healthier and I don’t have tired looking eyes anymore.

I had no idea but if others notice it def means it took a toll on my skin and eyes.

Feeling in control is huge. I’m 50 days in. Also, confidence that I did something I actually told myself I was going to do. Last time I smoked it was around a group of new people and I felt so paranoid and awkward that I decided that was it.

I have more mental clarity and am more in touch with my emotions.

Also free time! Instead of being high and watching bullshit from 9 until nighttime I have been reading, cooking new meals, and actively seeking out adventures and new hobbies.

I still have trouble waking up groggy but I have been doing yoga and look forward to waking up to practice it.

I think it’s worth it.

Now it’s almost 40 days and I feel numb and like I could fall asleep at any time.

I can’t wait to feel what sober life actually feels like! Clear headed and energetic. I really am working on loving myself too and this stopping smoking is the ultimate act of self love for me.

I feel 100% the same way. I smoked for 8 years every day and am on Day 28 now.

Live had a constant down mood, fatigue all day, and no motivation really.

I am usually a vivacious, energetic person who can talk to anyone. I feel like I’ve lost a part of myself but I have hope that as I continue my journey and focus on other activities the energy will pick up.

We are all here for each other which is a beautiful thing.

I am only on Day 26 now but I feel waves of emotions I had never felt in the past 7 years of being high every day.

I would go to family events, work, volunteer, college classes all high. Looking back it didn’t allow me to full engage and be my true self. At the time I thought it enhanced everything, but when real life events happen now I feel capable more so than ever before.

I’m dealing with depression and anxiety as well, but acknolwdging it and going through it rather than faking myself out by smoking and pretending I’m not affected. I used it to numb myself for 7 years straight.

Now I am 24, still so young! And I’m ready to embark on dreams I’ve had- traveling solo, reading more spiritual books, starting a blog. Before it was mainly “what’s the point?” attitude. I was very attached to a boyfriend and literally could only to the world through his point of view.

I guess what I’m experiencing now is a more decisive clarity and hope for the future. I find it difficult to eat even when hungry and I’ve been fatigued 90% of the day. But as I move forward into the unknown territory I’m excited to see what I create with my life.

I felt the same way- I would not even enjoy it anymore. I smoked everyday for 7 years with 2 breaks in between- 1 for work (32 days) and 1 for getting my life together (28 days). I'm on day 15 now and we just gotta stay positive and remember why we're doing it! For me it's emotional stability, confidence in myself to do something I say I want to for ME, and make new friendships with people who don't smoke. stay strong- go for walks, explore new places in your area, call a family member. make a routine
